narrative: Material PL1__MCE911A1 exhibits variable demand (CV=36.6%, mean 296.7 units/day) with no discernible trend over the 97-day observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=103.5%, mean 1.79 days), making lead-time variability the dominant source of uncertainty, accounting for 93.5% of total demand-during-lead-time variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 935 units and order quantity of 2,969 units was selected to achieve the 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by 79.7% versus the current SAP configuration.
warnings: Lead time CV > 100%: highly unstable supply chain; safety stock is sensitive to lead-time variability.
Storage constraint applied: unconstrained EOQ (2969) + safety stock (935) = 3904 <= 5067.782 — policy is feasible.
SAP safety stock is 0 — current policy has significant stockout risk.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Variable demand (CV=36.6%) and highly unstable lead times (CV=103.5%) require a responsive replenishment trigger. The (r,Q) policy monitors inventory continuously and fires a fixed EOQ-sized order when stock hits the reorder point, providing the best balance of service-level protection and cost efficiency for this material profile.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (77% utilised at 3,904 / 5,067.8 units). No capacity-driven order reduction was required. If demand grows >30%, capacity will become a constraint and order quantity will need to be split.
